g.text: Sign in on each computer. No Tailscale, no sshd, no open ports. TLS stays end to end, pinned to the host's key.
JWKS: the RS256 keys tokens are signed with
- relay/hosts via plxd A on sign-in, focus,
- Routes: LAN, relay 200 ms later, first wins
- Re-checks LAN every 60 s and on network change,
- plxd dial: accepts B's certificate only
if its key's JWK thumbprint == hostId
- DPoP key; one session per host after
- pinned-tls + TLS inside a relay stream (Work 5),
GET /connect/code: shows a sign-in code to paste
The relay can't read or change them.
Sees: Clerk tokens (T1), the host list, who is online
npx plx connect (run once on B)
1. Sign in: browser, or over SSH open the link
anywhere, allow, paste the code shown
4. Turn on relay and remote; approve the first
device with Enter when its code matches
Also: plx connect unlink | remove | status | add
- Host key P-256: hostId = JWK thumbprint
- Control WebSocket to the relay, opened
with a signed, single-use time proof
aud, client_id, sid, azp, exp, nbf)
iat within 60 s, own clock, 5 min skew
- Approved keys only: DPoP admin session,
PKCE, refresh: T1 for the relay,
LAN route, raced with the relay: direct TLS to B's :7341, same pin, no relay
1. A signs in to Clerk and holds T1.
2. plxd A asks the relay for the account's hosts (T1): B's hostId.
3. A tries B's LAN routes; 200 ms later, /connect with T1 too.
4. The relay joins A to B's spare stream to its :7341.
5. TLS 1.3 inside: B's key thumbprint must equal hostId.
6. A gets a fresh T2 and posts it with a DPoP proof to
7. B checks T2 against Clerk's JWKS and sub == its account.
8. A's key is new, so both show a code: Enter on B (plx
connect), Confirm on A. B issues a session for later.
The relay can't: read or change a stream (pinned TLS),
set B's account, or mint a session.
A compromised relay can list a fake host and catch a
token. The token alone gets nothing: an unknown key waits
until the user approves it once, matching a 6-digit code
from random values both sides commit to (1 in 10^6).
Still trusted: a brand-new device's first host, as in T3.
Other choices: sign-in alone (T3), or a pairing code
Removed one release after Work 3 and 5 ship
- connect setting, connect/devices, plxd connect on|off
- tailnet: routes on the desktop and the phone
- ssh to a Tailscale IP for installs and sign-ins
- connect on: relay and remote turn on, unless the user chose
- A tailnet: connection drops once the same key answers as
account:, matched by the JWK thumbprint of the reached cert
